subtitle: Pork simmered in lard
verso: In the copper cazo, the carnitas are never so-so.
story: In Quiroga, Michoacán, the carnitas capital, they're made in big copper cazos from Santa Clara del Cobre, the pork simmering in lard until it's tender inside and crisp outside. Orange and a splash of milk or Coke help it brown. It's party food for weekends, baptisms and birthdays.

ingredients.title: Carnitas
items: 5 lb pork shoulder, in 3-inch chunks (add some ribs or skin if you can)
2 lb lard (manteca), enough to almost cover
½ cup whole milk or Mexican Coca-Cola, optional

steps: Melt the lard in a heavy pot (cast iron or Dutch oven) over medium heat.
Add the pork, the salt, and the garlic and herbs if using. The lard should bubble gently, not fry hard. Cook 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the meat is tender.
Squeeze in the orange and drop in the halves. Add the milk or Coke. Cook 15 minutes.
Raise the heat to medium-high for the last 15–20 minutes so the pork turns golden brown and crisp at the edges. Watch for splatter.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain. Chop and serve with tortillas, salsa, onion, cilantro and lime.
Strain the lard when it cools and keep it in the fridge. It's gold for beans and tamales.

pressureCooker.time: 40 min high pressure + 15 min natural release, then broil
steps: Put the pork, salt, orange juice and halves, garlic, bay leaves, ½ cup water and [[3 tbsp]] lard in the pot.
Spread the meat on a sheet pan, break it into chunks, and drizzle with a few spoons of the fat and juices.
Broil 5–8 minutes until the edges crisp, or fry in batches in a hot cast-iron pan with lard.

tips: Ask the butcher for carnitas surtidas: maciza (lean), cuerito (skin), costilla (rib) and buche (stomach).
Don't stir much at first. Let the pork confit quietly.
Purists use only lard, salt and time. Orange, milk and Coca-Cola are carnitas makers' tricks for color, and every one has his own formula. If you use Coke, make it the cane-sugar Mexican one.
